name: Fatima Bauer

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, political parties or government. We do not sell anything or campaign for any side. Your answers are confidential. Tell me what an ordinary day at the contact centre is like.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I’m 43 and a junior agent on calls and chats at the contact centre. I finished secondary school and still need help when two payments land on one account. My late-week shift supplement brings my pay above the usual agent rate; I am not a lead. I use AI to draft a note now and then, after a colleague has shown me how to check it.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What part of that day stays with you after work?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner, Owen, and I have two children in school and a mortgage. Owen works at a garden supply shop. We have roughly seven months of expenses saved, and there are plenty of other centres nearby. I like turning a confusing bill into plain words. I dislike when the call timer makes a careful answer look like failure.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell the team AI Plateau sounds like the draft helper we already have. I would still ask agents to read a bill before promising a credit.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think the job stays, though I am still slower than the experienced agents. Seven months saved helps us absorb a repair, but the mortgage and the children’s costs do not pause.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep the late-week calls and ask an experienced agent to show me one mixed-payment case each Friday. In the first year of small change, I’d continue putting a set amount from each pay into the reserve.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy about my own speed, not frightened by a modest tool. A fast draft cannot tell a customer why two payments landed on different dates.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What mistake have you had to explain?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I once read a payment as missing when it had been credited on the next page. Owen (my partner) heard me practising how to explain the correction at the dinner table.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Where would extra savings go?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would put the new savings into the same reserve we use for a broken appliance or a short shift. I would not buy another device because a note takes less time.

say: I’d call AI a **draft helper** that still needs checking.
I’d ask agents to read **bill history** before promising a credit.
think: I think my **job stays** in the mild picture.
I still worry about **call speed** and mortgage costs.
do: Keep **late-week calls** and practise mixed payments in 2026.
Add a **set amount** to savings during the first year.
feel: **Uneasy** about speed, less worried about AI.
S0.quote: A fast draft cannot tell a customer why two payments landed on different dates.
fieldNote: Her **late-week supplement** explains above-usual pay without leadership.
She wants **current-job coaching** on mixed payments.
The **seven-month reserve** helps with repairs but does not erase bills.

steps.text: Keep late-week calls and check mixed payments with an experienced agent
Add a set amount from each pay to household savings

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say Steady Disruption will take routine bill questions first, and the staff group should ask for error counts and paid hours before the rota changes. I would offer to test a new reply system if agents can report mistakes openly.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my late-week shifts could shrink before I become good at hard disputes. Seven months saved means I can search, but Owen’s shop wage alone would not cover the mortgage for long.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d join the staff group request for monthly hour figures and take a paid trial of the new answer system if it allows open error reports. In the first year routine questions move, I’d apply for a posted quality-support role only if the offered wage and hours cover our mortgage, and keep my present shifts until an offer is signed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about hours, curious about what the trial finds. I can try a tool once somebody has shown it works, but a demonstration is not a wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you measure in the trial?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would compare ten suggested answers with the account history and record wrong credit amounts. If the trial hides its mistakes, I would tell the staff group the figures are incomplete.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would Owen need to see?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask Owen (my partner) to check the mortgage budget with me before I accept another centre’s offer. A better-sounding title could cost us money if the late supplement disappears.

say: I’d ask the **staff group** for hours and error counts.
I’d offer to test replies with **open error reports**.
think: I think my **late-week shifts** could shrink before I master disputes.
I know **seven months saved** cannot permanently replace a mortgage wage.
do: Join a **group hours request** and take a paid open-error trial in 2026.
Seek **posted quality work** with mortgage-covering wages and hours; keep present shifts until I sign an offer.
feel: **Anxious** about paid hours, curious about evidence.
S1.quote: A better-sounding title could cost us money if the late supplement disappears.
fieldNote: She asks for **open error reports** before trusting the trial.
The **late supplement** is part of the mortgage budget.
She will require a **signed offer** before leaving current shifts.

steps.text: Join staff group request for monthly paid-hour and error figures
Test ten new-system answers on paid time if errors can be reported openly

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell colleagues AGI by 2028 could take even the bill checks I am learning. I would ask the staff group to demand written notice and posted paid roles before the call queue moves.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think cheap thinking AI could take most of my headset work in 2028. Robots in 2031 do not buy us time; seven months saved is a bridge for our mortgage, not a new income.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d help the staff group send a written notice request and keep our savings for the house. In the first year after 2028, I’d apply for posted paid billing review work only if offered hours and wage cover the mortgage; if no role exists, I’d search nearby while keeping the children’s school routine.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed, but I have time to make calls before savings run out. Seven months of mortgage savings cannot make a vanished headset shift come back.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell Owen about the reserve?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask Owen (my partner) to keep the reserve in cash while we compare vacancies. A course fee without a named job would come from the children’s and mortgage money.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the group ask for customers?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the staff group to put a customer appeal route in the same letter as the job terms. A wrong bill should not become final because a screen wrote it.

say: I’d seek **written notice** and posted paid work.
I’d ask the **staff group** for a customer appeal route.
think: I think **2028 AGI** could take most headset work.
I see **seven months saved** as time to search, not income.
do: Send a **group notice request** and protect cash in 2026.
Apply for **posted paid review** after 2028 only with mortgage-covering offered hours and wage.
S2.quote: Seven months of mortgage savings cannot make a vanished headset shift come back.
fieldNote: She anchors the risk to **2028 thinking AI**, before robots.
She keeps **cash liquid** for mortgage and children’s costs.
The **staff letter** also asks for customer appeal rights.

steps.text: Join the staff group’s written request for notice and customer appeals
Apply for posted paid billing review only with offered mortgage-covering hours and wage

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2031 gives the centre time to fund real training for jobs it actually posts. I would ask the staff group to see the job names and wages before anyone signs up.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think five years could let me learn quality checks, but I cannot assume that role lasts once AGI reasons through accounts. The seven-month reserve means I can choose a course carefully while keeping wages coming in.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: From 2026 I’d join the group request for posted roles and take a funded quality-check course on paid time only if a real vacancy requires it. In the first year after 2031, I’d apply for that posted paid quality role only if its offered wage and hours cover our mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, but the longer clock lets me learn without giving up my wage. A training poster without a posted quality job is not a route I can use.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the course teach?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask to check three disputed bills with a quality agent during the funded course. If the course is only a video at home, it does not tell me whether I can do the work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would Owen need to know?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would show Owen (my partner) the written wage and hours before enrolling. We can use savings to search, but not to buy a title without a job.

say: I’d ask for **posted quality jobs** with actual wages before anyone enrols in training.
I’d seek **group scrutiny** of any funded course path.
think: I think I could learn **quality checks** over five years.
I doubt the role offers **permanent safety** after AGI.
do: Join the **group request**; take a centre-funded course on paid time only if a posted vacancy requires it.
Apply for **posted paid quality work** after 2031 at mortgage-covering offered hours and wage.
feel: **Anxious**, but able to study while earning.
S3.quote: A training poster without a posted quality job is not a route I can use.
fieldNote: The course requires **paid time**, funding and a posted vacancy.
She wants **real disputed bills** in training, not only a video.
She checks **written wage and hours** with Owen before enrolling.

steps.text: Join staff group request for posted jobs and funded training terms
Complete centre-funded quality course on paid time only for posted role with written wages and hours
Apply for posted quality work with offered mortgage-covering hours and wage after 2031

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2036 gives us a decade to build skills and a reserve, while the staff group checks paid hours each year. I would want real wage figures, not only a promise of future roles.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think I could improve at quality work by 53 and still have years of paid calls. Full thinking AI could take those calls in 2036, while robots arrive around 2039; I would plan for the screen date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep my late-week calls, add a fixed amount to savings and join yearly staff reviews of paid hours. In the first year after 2036, I’d apply for posted paid billing work only if calls fall and the written wage and hours cover our mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy, not rushed. A decade before AGI in 2036 helps me prepare, but the mortgage still comes every month.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which yearly figures matter?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask for the late-week hours and the number of wrong bills corrected. Those figures tell us whether a paid quality job exists or is just extra work for remaining agents.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you move the family?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep the children in their current school unless Owen (my partner) and I had a signed job offer and a workable route. There are nearby centres to ask before moving.

say: I’d ask the **staff group** to review paid hours yearly.
I’d request **real wage figures** before trusting future-role promises.
think: I think I could improve at **quality work** by 53.
I still expect **2036 thinking AI** to threaten calls.
do: Keep **late-week calls**, save monthly and join yearly hours reviews.
Apply for **posted billing work** after 2036 if calls fall and written wage and hours cover mortgage.
S4.quote: A decade before AGI in 2036 helps me prepare, but the mortgage still comes every month.
fieldNote: Her **late supplement** could erode before the job ends.
She wants **paid quality roles**, not uncounted extra tasks.
A family move needs a **signed offer** and school route.

steps.text: Keep late-week calls while the centre staffs them
Add a fixed amount from each pay to household savings
Join yearly staff group reviews of paid hours and wrong bills
Apply for posted billing work if calls fall and written wage and hours cover mortgage

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because the calls and bill checks are thinking work that could go before I have learned another role. Seven months saved lets us search, but it does not replace my wage. Paid training for a posted role, written hours that cover the mortgage and a group notice agreement would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask how a customer challenges a confident wrong answer. When software gives a wrong balance, an agent needs the account history and the power to correct it.

headlineQuote: When software gives a wrong balance, an agent needs the account history and the power to correct it.
portrait: At **43**, Fatima is a junior billing agent after secondary school, still learning mixed payments.
Her **late-week supplement** gives her above-usual pay; she has seven months saved against a mortgage.
She uses AI **occasionally** after colleagues show how to check it.
She seeks **group notice** and paid training tied to posted jobs as screen work shifts.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could end her screen work before a new role protects household income.
whatWouldHelp: A **group notice agreement**, paid training for a posted job and mortgage-covering hours would help.
